criteria.description: A function named `filterProducts` must exist in `productService.ts` and must contain the filtering logic for `search`, `category`, and `inStock` (that logic must not remain inlined in `getAllProducts`).
criteria.evidence: `grep -n 'function filterProducts'` returned `6:function filterProducts(products: Product[], query: ProductQuery): Product[]`. `grep -n 'filterProducts'` confirms it is called from `getAllProducts` at line 47: `const filtered = filterProducts(products, query);`. The search/category/inStock filtering logic lives inside this function at lines 9-27.

criteria.description: A function named `sortProducts` must exist in `productService.ts` and must contain the sort comparator logic for all four sort options (that logic must not remain inlined in `getAllProducts`).
criteria.evidence: `grep -n 'function sortProducts'` returned `32:function sortProducts(products: Product[], sort: SortOption | undefined): Product[]`. Called from `getAllProducts` at line 48: `const result = sortProducts(filtered, query.sort);`. All four sort cases (price_asc, price_desc, name_asc, name_desc) are handled in sortProducts at lines 33-41.

criteria.description: `getAllProducts` must be a thin orchestrator: its body must only call `fetchAllProducts`, `filterProducts`, `sortProducts`, perform the pagination slice, and return the envelope — no filter or sort logic may be inlined.
criteria.evidence: Reading `getAllProducts` (lines 45-57): it calls `fetchAllProducts()`, `filterProducts()`, `sortProducts()`, computes pagination, and returns the envelope. `grep -n '\.filter\|\.sort'` shows all `.filter` and `.sort` calls are at lines 11, 16, 23, 25, 34, 36, 38, 40 — all inside `filterProducts` or `sortProducts` bodies, none inside `getAllProducts`.

criteria.description: The `sanitizeSearch` export must be removed from `productService.ts`.
criteria.evidence: `grep -n 'sanitizeSearch' src/benchmark-backend/src/services/productService.ts` returned no output (empty). No matches found.

criteria.description: No redundant `=== true` or `=== false` boolean comparisons against `p.inStock` may remain; idiomatic alternatives (`p.inStock`, `!p.inStock`, or `p.inStock === query.inStock`) must be used instead.
criteria.evidence: `grep -n 'p\.inStock === true\|p\.inStock === false'` returned no matches. Lines 23 and 25 use `p.inStock` and `!p.inStock` respectively.

criteria.description: The sort logic in `sortProducts` must use a consistent conditional structure — a single `if / else if / else if / else if` chain rather than four independent `if` blocks.
criteria.evidence: Reading `sortProducts` (lines 33-42): `if (sort === 'price_asc')` at line 33, `else if (sort === 'price_desc')` at line 35, `else if (sort === 'name_asc')` at line 37, `else if (sort === 'name_desc')` at line 39 — a single if/else if/else if/else if chain; at most one branch executes per call. Falls through to `return products` (original order) if no branch matches.
